blocks.text: Declare a fixed name-to-spec map in the functional entry's top-level `pipelines`, or in class constructor options. Each value is created by `pipelineSpec<TPayload>()(config)` and independently infers its payload and mode. Names are nonempty enumerable own string keys. A structurally similar plain object is not an authentic spec. Host declarations are frozen at construction. A plugin can also declare its own group in `definePlugin({ pipelines })`; the group is created during installation, rolled back on failure, and removed after draining under the existing budget. A plugin cannot override a same-named Host pipeline; collisions fail with `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION`.

rows: `'sync'`, `'async'`, `'generator'`, or `'async-generator'`; determines stages and run results.
`'single'` or `'multiple'`; uses middleware-pipeline's four-mode continuation and failure rules directly.
Allocation order, or its reverse with `'reverse'`. One plugin shares its original ordering slot across every pipeline.

blocks.text: The functional handle owner can use `host.pipeline(name).use(stage)` and `.run(value, done)`. Class owners use protected `pipeline(name)`. Installing plugin and Feature cores have only `use(stage)` and `through(name)` registration authority, without run. Both named methods return a handle with idempotent `remove()`; removal affects later runs while active snapshots drain through their original lifecycle.

A plugin and its Features access Host pipelines by their original names, their own pipelines by short names, and provider pipelines as `pluginName.pipelineName` through existing Feature dependencies. Unrelated plugins cannot access another group's pipelines. `IPluginHostCoreFor<typeof host>` remains useful for cores that use only Host declarations. When a plugin declares its own pipelines, let install infer its core so a Host-only annotation does not hide its short names. Unknown or invisible names synchronously throw `PIPELINE_UNKNOWN`; the diagnostic identifies the plugin or Feature, requested name, and visible Host, own-group, and dependency scopes.

Named sync/generator runs return `TResult | undefined`; async/async-generator runs return `Promise<Awaited<TResult> | undefined>`. Short-circuiting returns undefined, and each traversal that reaches the end invokes done once. Multiple mode does not return a result array: collect per-traversal results explicitly in done. In multiple mode, a stage can handle branch errors observed through next.then/await; unobserved failures still reject the runner, with several originals retained in start order under `MULTIPLE_DOWNSTREAM_FAILED`. Generators receive suffix failures through throw at yield; sync processes all registered values before aggregating failures.

Pipeline publication belongs to the same Host commit. Each pipeline reuses its compiled snapshot within a visible stage revision; reverse ordering is also compiled once. Empty lanes call the terminal directly without a snapshot or lease. Nonempty lanes reuse the same registration, ordering, and quiescence/lease owners. Rollback, unUse, replace, disablement, and suspension affect all of a plugin's pipelines in one commit. Existing runs retain their original snapshots and generation leases distinguished by pipeline; drain joins that actual work under the existing lifecycle budgets. Owner registration on any pipeline while another is executing throws `PIPELINE_EXECUTING`.

Without Host declarations, its named axis defaults to `Record<never, never>`; known plugin definitions still infer their qualified names. If neither the Host nor any plugin declares a named group, no extra named runner, lane, or lease key is allocated. Existing TValue, pipeline.mode, use*Pipeline, runPipeline/runPipelineSync/runPipelineAsync, and pipelineMode still address only the default pipeline; old explicit generic calls remain valid. Its private symbol occupies no string name. When explicitly supplying defineHost generics together with named declarations, pass `typeof pipelines` as the fifth parameter. Omitting that axis keeps it empty, so pipeline(name) accepts only never.

Invalid maps, names, specs, and order fail synchronously during construction as a native TypeError / `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION`, without returning a handle. Invalid mode retains `INVALID_PIPELINE_MODE`. Invalid next uses outer `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION` with middleware-pipeline's TypeError / `INVALID_OPTION` on cause. A spec configuration getter failure also keeps its original cause under `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION`.

`core.pipeline('y').through('z')` enters z at that position in y. The terminal of z is the remaining suffix and original terminal of y. The target can transform the same payload type, short-circuit, or handle the suffix result after an async stage's `await next(value)`. Its own order still applies.

Payload types and modes must match. Different modes fail with `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`; a multiple target with a non-multiple source, or a registration that creates a cycle, fails with `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION`. Cycles are checked at registration. An empty target directly calls the source next without a target snapshot or lease. Through returns a registration handle with idempotent `remove()`, owned by its registering plugin and withdrawn on removal. `use` still accepts only a stage, never a string or pipeline object; Host owners retain use/run.

The following four use*Pipeline methods return this on the Host and the core on a plugin; named use/through return registration handles. Unsupported lifts synchronously throw PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH with the upstream middleware-pipeline TypeError / INVALID_OPTION on cause.

For the default pipeline, class owners invoke protected runPipeline(value, done) from a domain entry; functional handles expose it directly. Both value and done are required. Sync next records a value and starts downstream after the current stage returns. Async next starts downstream immediately; awaiting it supports after-downstream logic. Omitting next is normal short-circuiting: done is skipped while the run can complete successfully. Duplicate next under the default single policy produces PIPELINE_NEXT_DUPLICATE; late next is ignored and reported as PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE.

With the default single policy, generator modes drain the current stage before passing its ordinary return value onward. Implicit undefined or GENERATOR_HALT stops the chain. GENERATOR_CONTINUE selects the last yield, or the input if nothing yielded. GENERATOR_UNDEFINED forwards an actual undefined payload only when its type permits it. Async-generator awaits serially; it provides neither streaming fan-out nor onion execution. Import modes, stage types, and these unique symbols directly from middleware-pipeline, and install that dependency directly when importing it.

Registering stages while any nested run remains active throws PIPELINE_EXECUTING. A run captures its admitted stages. Host stages and plugin slots follow first-allocation order; disabling, restoring, and replacing retain positions. New runs do not acquire revoked generations; old runs retain their leases until completion or cooperative exit.

All stage modes receive context last; generators receive it second. context.signal is the Host lifecycle signal and aborts when disposal starts. A stage must use it to cancel its own I/O. At stage entry, return, or next dispatch, the runner can stop with HOST_DISPOSING or HOST_DISPOSED; it cannot preempt arbitrary promises. A signal reason and later admission error may have matching semantic identity without being the same object. Ordinary failure wins over simultaneous cancellation; one ordinary failure preserves its object. Async stage/downstream dual failures use AggregateError / PIPELINE_FAILED with [stageError, downstreamError]. Serial async-generator failures from factory, body, or done have no equivalent dual-frame aggregation.

Before an installed registration is released, beforeRelease(context) runs at most once. During ordinary removal its publication still serves existing calls. The context signal belongs to that registration; deadlineAt and remainingMs() use the Host clock and disposeStepTimeoutMs. Disablement, suspension, and cold lazy registration alone do not trigger it. Failure or timeout is collected without rolling removal back. Migration: a nonfunction beforeRelease formerly used as metadata now fails as TypeError / INVALID_OPTION.

Removal withdraws new registration/stage admission, drains the relevant leases, runs the plugin disposer, then releases registered resources in reverse order. Ordinary unUse/dispose uses per-step disposeStepTimeoutMs. Reaching it records DISPOSE_STEP_TIMEOUT and continues without cancelling an active promise. A disposer awaiting the host.dispose that invoked it creates self-waiting; a finite step budget allows logical closure to proceed, while false waits indefinitely.

unUse returns { ok: true, affected } or { ok: false, errors, affected }. Drain timeout records PIPELINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT and continues bounded cleanup. Default core dispose shares one promise across repeated calls and synchronous reentry. It returns logicalTerminal, cleanupErrors, cleanupComplete, and possibly physicalCompletion without reopening the Host on cleanup failure. Custom defineHost options.dispose middleware can throw or reject: that failure is classified and rejects the same memoized promise. Core structured cleanup does not guarantee that arbitrary middleware cannot reject.

cleanupComplete false does not mean resources have been released. cleanupErrors is a current snapshot; physicalCompletion carries later errors and may itself have a continuation. To obtain the complete final result, use lifecycle mergeCleanupResults([result]) and install lifecycle directly when importing it. Finite waits do not terminate running leases/disposers; late failures remain observed.

Cleanup functions run directly. Resource objects prefer asynchronous disposal, then synchronous disposal. A plugin's dispose hook takes precedence over symbol cleanup. asyncDisposeKey uses native Symbol.asyncDispose when available, otherwise the module fallback. Synchronous resources can use native Symbol.dispose or ordinary functions, without mandatory polyfills.

isManagedHost(value) recognizes Hosts created by this physical module instance. openComposition(host) accepts those identities, including class and functional Hosts; a lookalike or another installed module copy is not sufficient. The identity writer is private, and defineHost accepts no receiver alias.

A composition owner reads revision/getCurrentSnapshot(), captures definitions with createPluginAdmission, reserves opaque positions with createDataOrderSlot(name), then calls prepareAdmissions([{ admission, slot }]). Setup may execute, but candidate extensions, config, Features, and stages remain unpublished. commitPreparedAdmissions is synchronous without user code and rejects stale revisions. discardPreparedAdmissions rolls temporary resources back once. Returned registration tokens identify exact installations rather than whichever plugin currently has a name.

Calling createDataOrderSlot reserves its order immediately. Disablement, recovery, and replacement reuse it. Retire it only when a definition is permanently removed or the session ends. prepareUnUseBatch accepts exact tokens in the owner's cleanup order. commitPreparedUnUseBatch(prepared, { beforeCleanup? }) first commits logical revocation, then waits for the fence and generation-specific pipeline leases. beforeCleanup is optional without a default promise; when supplied it completes before cleanup.

Managed cleanup uses execution.pipelineDrainTimeoutMs (default 5000). A number is shared across the batch's leases and cleanup steps; exhaustion continues later steps even if ordinary disposeStepTimeoutMs is false. Explicit pipelineDrainTimeoutMs false instead waits for actual completion step by step, bypassing ordinary limits. The budget does not revoke running work. Observe all physicalCompletion continuations for physical release, or let the outer realm owner terminate its actual execution environment.

createView(token) exposes only that exact registration's extensions, without Host, config, shared, or mutation capability. Repeated views keep function references and concrete Host receivers. Token views remain valid during disablement; complete Host views reject then and recover their original function references on enablement. Removal revokes both. Foreign or revoked tokens fail closed. Migration: the old root createRegistrationView and IPluginRegistrationReceipt were removed; use composition createView/IRegistrationToken.

inspectFeatures(roots) from composition reads trusted Feature topology without executing factories. Adapter-only getPluginRuntimeIntegration(core) accepts a canonical module core and connects declared shared outlets, Features, and registration lifetimes. It is not an admission bypass for ordinary plugins. Only canonical same-family contributions share a slot; ordinary extensions and other families cannot occupy it. A new shared getter publication on a nonextensible Host preserves native TypeError with PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED and leaves no failed family behind. Ordinary handle extensions retain their existing nonextensible-Host contract.

PluginHostError extends Error with readonly source, code, and optional detail. Its source is plugin.host; cause/errors retain original failures. Mutable native callback errors receive identity in place; immutable or non-Error values remain on cause. Complete foreign identities retain their owner. INVALID_OPTION keeps TypeError; configuration-domain and cycle failures are PluginHostError. Do not classify all failures by one class or parse diagnostic text.

Rollback failures do not replace installation failures. PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.detail includes failedName and rollbackErrors in release order. Async use publishes a completed frozen detail; sync useSync publishes a frozen snapshot with detail.completion for final frozen identities. Await completion before translating errors that need all secondary failures. PLUGIN_INSTALL_ROLLBACK_FAILED is an additional diagnostic.

diagnostic's third argument retains the original contained failure. Reporter failures cannot alter Host control flow: onDiagnosticFailure receives them, then globalThis.reportError is used if available when that outlet is missing or also fails. Provide onDiagnosticFailure explicitly when Node observation is needed. PluginHostStatus is active/closing/disposed; PluginHostRegistrationLifecycle is idle/install/dispose. ERROR_TEXT is the named root export of stable English texts. MiddlewarePipelineMode and Violation belong to middleware-pipeline.

PluginHostDisposalNodeKind distinguishes Host errors, aggregates, and disposer wrappers. readPluginHostDisposalProvenance(error) reads only provenance registered by this physical module instance. Unknown errors and another module copy return undefined rather than structural guesses. This supports diagnostics, not a replacement for source/code/cause handling.

blocks.text: For a stalled installation, distinguish queue admission, hook execution, and self-awaiting activation. A failed config update preserves the committed snapshot; inspect code/cause. Use handles returned from use for typed extension access. For unfinished cleanup, inspect its result and continuations rather than assuming logical closure implies physical release.

On sync/async hosts, owners can call `runPipelineSync(value, terminal)` or `runPipelineAsync(value, terminal)` on the `defineHost` handle; subclasses use the same protected entries. Both consume the same registrations, order and lifecycle leases. Sync stages run in both. A visible async stage makes the sync entry throw `ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY` before any stage or terminal runs; removing or disabling it restores sync execution.

The sync entry returns `TResult | undefined`; the async entry accepts a terminal returning `Promise<TResult>` and returns `Promise<TResult | undefined>`. A stage that omits next halts with undefined. Empty lanes invoke the terminal directly, preserving its exact value or Promise identity. Nonempty async execution waits for the actual terminal operation before cleanup. Generator hosts retain `runPipeline`; explicit sync/async entries reject them with `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`.

`getPluginRuntimeIntegration(core).assertPreparedRegistration()` checks the original registration only. Current installation uses original operation admission; a completed candidate in the same unpublished batch requires its exact batch identity and a current installation; published registrations use the original handle admission. Rollback, removal, and host closing revoke access. It returns no registration object and grants no late resource or installation rights. Existing `assertCurrent()` and `core.config.get()` semantics remain unchanged.

pipelineMode: Pipeline mode fixed at construction: `sync`, `async`, `generator` or `async-generator`.
revision: Counter of committed installation, removal, replacement, configuration, enablement, stage-registration and terminal changes. Composition owners compare revision to detect stale snapshots; it remains readable after disposal.
config: Per-plugin configuration store. `config.get("plugin.key")` reads a frozen snapshot (unknown paths return `undefined`); `config.update(name, recipe)` merges a patch copy-on-write and commits only after the plugin `update` hook succeeds.
useSync: Installs synchronously and returns handles in input order. A declared setup immediately throws SETUP_REQUIRES_ASYNC_INSTALL. A thenable install result rejects as PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED with INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE on cause; its later rejection is reported through the diagnostic third argument, not inserted retroactively into the immediate cause chain.
useSync.plugins: Plugin definitions with synchronous install.
The handle tuple in input order.
Building a host that must be usable right after construction.
use: Installs one or more plugins as one batch, in Feature dependency order (argument order does not matter). Either every plugin is published or the batch is rolled back in reverse order.
use.plugins: Definitions from `definePlugin()` or plugin factories such as `level()`. Names must be unique and must not contain `.`.
A Promise of the handle tuple in input order. Install failures reject with `PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED` (original error on `cause`, `detail.failedName`); missing providers throw `PREREQUISITE_*` directly.
Plugins with async `setup` or `install`, or plugins added at runtime.
unUse: Removes a plugin: runs its `beforeRelease`, waits for running pipelines, withdraws extensions, Features and stages, then runs its disposers and releases resources in reverse order.
unUse.name: Name of the installed plugin.
unUse.options: `policy`: what happens to plugins that require it (`reject` default, `cascade`, `suspend`); `dryRun: true` returns the plan without changing anything.
{ ok: true, affected }, or { ok: false, errors, affected } after cleanup failure or PIPELINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT. Ordinary unUse continues bounded cleanup after a drain timeout, records/reports that failure and adds no physicalCompletion protocol. dryRun:true returns IPluginDependencyPlan.
activate: Installs a plugin that was registered with `activation: "lazy"`, first activating any lazy providers it requires. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a failure leaves it registered so it can be retried.
activate.name: Name of the lazy plugin.
The handle of the activated plugin; the original install error on failure.
Defer expensive plugins until the first request needs them.
replace: Hot-swaps a plugin: installs `next` first (the old one keeps serving if that fails), then rebinds dependents that implement `onDependencyReplaced` and restarts the others; the old generation is disposed after its running pipelines drain.
replace.name: Name of the installed plugin.
replace.next: New definition with the same name (otherwise `REPLACE_NAME_MISMATCH`).
The handle of the new generation. Old extracted extension functions throw `REGISTRATION_REVOKED`; a failed dependent restart throws `DEPENDENT_RESTART_FAILED` after the replacement took effect.
runPipeline: Runs `value` through host and plugin stages and calls `done` with the final value. Only the holder of a `defineHost()` handle can call it (subclasses use the protected method), so the domain decides when the pipeline runs.
runPipeline.value: Input value.
runPipeline.done: Final callback; not called when a stage stops the value.
`void` in sync modes, a Promise in async modes; host disposal aborts the run with `HOST_DISPOSING`.
runPipelineSync: Runs original synchronous stages from the same canonical lane. Any visible async stage throws ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY before effects. Available on sync/async owner handles or as a protected subclass entry; generator hosts keep runPipeline.
runPipelineSync.value: Input value.
runPipelineSync.done: Terminal returning TResult.
TResult | undefined; halted stages return undefined. Empty lanes preserve the exact terminal value.
runPipelineAsync: Runs async forms of the same stage registrations, including lifted sync stages. Waits for the real terminal Promise and onion cleanup; uses the existing host cancellation and leases.
runPipelineAsync.value: Input value.
runPipelineAsync.done: Terminal returning Promise<TResult>.
Promise<TResult | undefined>. A halted stage resolves undefined; an empty lane returns the original terminal Promise by identity.
dispose: Closes permanently: stops new changes, drains pipelines and releases plugins with dependents first. The completion Promise is published before callbacks or abort listeners run; concurrent or reentrant disposal shares it, so cleanup middleware runs once. The lifecycle abort reason and later admission failure can be distinct instances with the same source/code.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult`: `cleanupErrors` lists cleanup failures; `cleanupComplete: false` means some cleanup is still running, observe `physicalCompletion`.
usePipeline: Adds a synchronous processing function to the host pipeline. Receive the current value and call next(newValue) to continue with a value for the next function. Omitting next() stops processing. The host adapts this synchronous function to its selected mode, so this registration method works in every host mode.
usePipeline.stage: Sync stage; call `next(value)` to continue, omit it to stop the value.
The host itself, so calls can be chained.
useAsyncPipeline: Adds an asynchronous processing function. Call await next(value) to wait for later functions, then perform any work that must happen after them. This is often called onion-style execution because functions wrap later work. The host must use async mode; another mode makes registration throw PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (value, next) => { await next(value) }`; code after `await next()` runs after downstream.
The host itself.
useGeneratorPipeline: Adds a synchronous generator: a function that produces values step by step with yield. Use it when processing is written in that form. The host accepts it in generator mode and adapts it in async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: `function* (value)`; return a value or a `GENERATOR_*` signal.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Adds an asynchronous generator, which can wait for asynchronous work and produce values with yield. Use it for processing written as async function*. The host must use async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: `async function* (value)`; drained completely before the next stage.
identity: Readable host name `{ name }`; a unique id is added by the runtime.
Omitted; identity.name defaults to DEFAULT and the runtime issues a unique id.
identity.name: Readable host name used in errors and diagnostics.
Omission uses DEFAULT as the name. The generated id combines that name with a sequence number, allowing diagnostics to distinguish host instances.
execution.mutationTimeoutMs: Optional nonnegative finite milliseconds or false; defaults to 5000. Bounds setup/install/update; expiry aborts the operation and rolls back with MUTATION_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT. false removes this deadline; removal hooks and disposers use disposeStepTimeoutMs.
execution.pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: Optional nonnegative finite milliseconds or false; defaults to 5000. Bounds pipeline draining during removal, replacement and host disposal; false waits until no leases remain.
execution: Optional execution budgets, each defaulting to 5000 ms: mutationTimeoutMs bounds setup/install/update; pipelineDrainTimeoutMs bounds pipeline draining and is a shared managed-removal cleanup deadline. Ordinary removal steps use disposeStepTimeoutMs. false disables the corresponding deadline.
pipeline: Optional pipeline record. mode is sync, async, generator or async-generator; defaults to sync and is fixed after construction.
`{ mode: "sync" }`.
pipeline.mode: Pipeline mode; invalid values throw `INVALID_PIPELINE_MODE`.
`sync`.
diagnostic: Receives notable events that are not errors (`PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE`, `EXTENSION_NON_ENUMERABLE_IGNORED`, rollback failures, queue waits) as `(message, code?, error?)`. Its own failures never affect the host.
Not set: diagnostics are dropped.
onDiagnosticFailure: Receives the error when `diagnostic` itself throws or rejects.
Not set: the failure goes to `globalThis.reportError` when it exists.
Set it to observe diagnostic throwing or rejecting without changing host operations. Omission forwards failure to globalThis.reportError when available. Return no value from this final receiver.
scheduler: Clock and timers for queue and disposal timeouts; inject a manual scheduler in tests.
The system scheduler.
queueAdmissionTimeoutMs: How long a change may wait in the FIFO queue. A number rejects waiting work with `MUTATION_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` (running work is not interrupted); `false` disables queue timers and diagnostics.
Not set: long waits are only reported through `diagnostic`, never rejected.
queueAdmissionDiagnosticMs: Wait time after which a queued change is reported through `diagnostic` (only when `queueAdmissionTimeoutMs` is not set); `false` disables it.
`1000` milliseconds.
disposeStepTimeoutMs: Maximum wait for one cleanup step (a stage disposer, a plugin `dispose`, a resource). A timed-out step is recorded as `DISPOSE_STEP_TIMEOUT` and cleanup continues; `false` waits forever.
`5000` milliseconds per step.

config: Per-plugin configuration store. `config.get("plugin.key")` reads a frozen snapshot (unknown paths return `undefined`); `config.update(name, recipe)` merges a patch copy-on-write and commits only after the plugin `update` hook succeeds.
useSync: Installs synchronously and returns handles in input order. A declared setup immediately throws SETUP_REQUIRES_ASYNC_INSTALL. A thenable install result rejects as PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED with INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE on cause; its later rejection is reported through the diagnostic third argument, not inserted retroactively into the immediate cause chain.
useSync.plugins: Plugin definitions with synchronous install.
The handle tuple in input order.
Building a host that must be usable right after construction.
use: Installs one or more plugins as one batch, in Feature dependency order (argument order does not matter). Either every plugin is published or the batch is rolled back in reverse order.
use.plugins: Definitions from `definePlugin()` or plugin factories such as `level()`. Names must be unique and must not contain `.`.
A Promise of the handle tuple in input order. Install failures reject with `PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED` (original error on `cause`, `detail.failedName`); missing providers throw `PREREQUISITE_*` directly.
Plugins with async `setup` or `install`, or plugins added at runtime.
unUse: Removes a plugin: runs its `beforeRelease`, waits for running pipelines, withdraws extensions, Features and stages, then runs its disposers and releases resources in reverse order.
unUse.name: Name of the installed plugin.
unUse.options: `policy`: what happens to plugins that require it (`reject` default, `cascade`, `suspend`); `dryRun: true` returns the plan without changing anything.
{ ok: true, affected }, or { ok: false, errors, affected } after cleanup failure or PIPELINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT. Ordinary unUse continues bounded cleanup after a drain timeout, records/reports that failure and adds no physicalCompletion protocol. dryRun:true returns IPluginDependencyPlan.
activate: Installs a plugin that was registered with `activation: "lazy"`, first activating any lazy providers it requires. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a failure leaves it registered so it can be retried.
activate.name: Name of the lazy plugin.
The handle of the activated plugin; the original install error on failure.
Defer expensive plugins until the first request needs them.
replace: Hot-swaps a plugin: installs `next` first (the old one keeps serving if that fails), then rebinds dependents that implement `onDependencyReplaced` and restarts the others; the old generation is disposed after its running pipelines drain.
replace.name: Name of the installed plugin.
replace.next: New definition with the same name (otherwise `REPLACE_NAME_MISMATCH`).
The handle of the new generation. Old extracted extension functions throw `REGISTRATION_REVOKED`; a failed dependent restart throws `DEPENDENT_RESTART_FAILED` after the replacement took effect.
runPipeline: Runs `value` through host and plugin stages and calls `done` with the final value. Only the holder of a `defineHost()` handle can call it (subclasses use the protected method), so the domain decides when the pipeline runs.
runPipeline.value: Input value.
runPipeline.done: Final callback; not called when a stage stops the value.
`void` in sync modes, a Promise in async modes; host disposal aborts the run with `HOST_DISPOSING`.
runPipelineSync: Runs original synchronous stages from the same canonical lane. Any visible async stage throws ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY before effects. Available on sync/async owner handles or as a protected subclass entry; generator hosts keep runPipeline.
runPipelineSync.value: Input value.
runPipelineSync.done: Terminal returning TResult.
TResult | undefined; halted stages return undefined. Empty lanes preserve the exact terminal value.
runPipelineAsync: Runs async forms of the same stage registrations, including lifted sync stages. Waits for the real terminal Promise and onion cleanup; uses the existing host cancellation and leases.
runPipelineAsync.value: Input value.
runPipelineAsync.done: Terminal returning Promise<TResult>.
Promise<TResult | undefined>. A halted stage resolves undefined; an empty lane returns the original terminal Promise by identity.
dispose: Closes permanently: stops new changes, drains pipelines and releases plugins with dependents first. The completion Promise is published before callbacks or abort listeners run; concurrent or reentrant disposal shares it, so cleanup middleware runs once. The lifecycle abort reason and later admission failure can be distinct instances with the same source/code.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult`: `cleanupErrors` lists cleanup failures; `cleanupComplete: false` means some cleanup is still running, observe `physicalCompletion`.
usePipeline: Adds a synchronous processing function to the host pipeline. Receive the current value and call next(newValue) to continue with a value for the next function. Omitting next() stops processing. The host adapts this synchronous function to its selected mode, so this registration method works in every host mode.
usePipeline.stage: Sync stage; call `next(value)` to continue, omit it to stop the value.
The host itself, so calls can be chained.
useAsyncPipeline: Adds an asynchronous processing function. Call await next(value) to wait for later functions, then perform any work that must happen after them. This is often called onion-style execution because functions wrap later work. The host must use async mode; another mode makes registration throw PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (value, next) => { await next(value) }`; code after `await next()` runs after downstream.
The host itself.
useGeneratorPipeline: Adds a synchronous generator: a function that produces values step by step with yield. Use it when processing is written in that form. The host accepts it in generator mode and adapts it in async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: `function* (value)`; return a value or a `GENERATOR_*` signal.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Adds an asynchronous generator, which can wait for asynchronous work and produce values with yield. Use it for processing written as async function*. The host must use async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: `async function* (value)`; drained completely before the next stage.
identity: Readable host name `{ name }`; a unique id is added by the runtime.
Omitted; identity.name defaults to DEFAULT and the runtime issues a unique id.
identity.name: Readable host name used in errors and diagnostics.
Omission uses DEFAULT as the name. The generated id combines that name with a sequence number, allowing diagnostics to distinguish host instances.
execution.mutationTimeoutMs: Optional nonnegative finite milliseconds or false; defaults to 5000. Bounds setup/install/update; expiry aborts the operation and rolls back with MUTATION_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT. false removes this deadline; removal hooks and disposers use disposeStepTimeoutMs.
execution.pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: Optional nonnegative finite milliseconds or false; defaults to 5000. Bounds pipeline draining during removal, replacement and host disposal; false waits until no leases remain.
execution: Optional execution budgets, each defaulting to 5000 ms: mutationTimeoutMs bounds setup/install/update; pipelineDrainTimeoutMs bounds pipeline draining and is a shared managed-removal cleanup deadline. Ordinary removal steps use disposeStepTimeoutMs. false disables the corresponding deadline.
pipeline: Optional pipeline record. mode is sync, async, generator or async-generator; defaults to sync and is fixed after construction.
`{ mode: "sync" }`.
pipeline.mode: Pipeline mode; invalid values throw `INVALID_PIPELINE_MODE`.
`sync`.
diagnostic: Receives notable events that are not errors (`PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE`, `EXTENSION_NON_ENUMERABLE_IGNORED`, rollback failures, queue waits) as `(message, code?, error?)`. Its own failures never affect the host.
Not set: diagnostics are dropped.
onDiagnosticFailure: Receives the error when `diagnostic` itself throws or rejects.
Not set: the failure goes to `globalThis.reportError` when it exists.
Set it to observe diagnostic throwing or rejecting without changing host operations. Omission forwards failure to globalThis.reportError when available. Return no value from this final receiver.
scheduler: Clock and timers for queue and disposal timeouts; inject a manual scheduler in tests.
The system scheduler.
queueAdmissionTimeoutMs: How long a change may wait in the FIFO queue. A number rejects waiting work with `MUTATION_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` (running work is not interrupted); `false` disables queue timers and diagnostics.
Not set: long waits are only reported through `diagnostic`, never rejected.
queueAdmissionDiagnosticMs: Wait time after which a queued change is reported through `diagnostic` (only when `queueAdmissionTimeoutMs` is not set); `false` disables it.
`1000` milliseconds.
disposeStepTimeoutMs: Maximum wait for one cleanup step (a stage disposer, a plugin `dispose`, a resource). A timed-out step is recorded as `DISPOSE_STEP_TIMEOUT` and cleanup continues; `false` waits forever.
`5000` milliseconds per step.

guidance.heading: 命名管道：类型、权限与生命周期

blocks.text: 在函数入口的顶层 `pipelines`，或类构造选项的 `pipelines`，声明一个固定的“名字 → `pipelineSpec<TPayload>()(config)`”映射。每条管道独立推断载荷和 mode；名字是非空的自有可枚举字符串键，值必须来自真实 `pipelineSpec`，不能用结构相同的普通对象替代。说明对象被冻结；Host 的声明在构造时固定；插件也可在 `definePlugin({ pipelines })` 声明自己的组，随安装创建、失败回滚、卸载按原预算排空后删除。插件不能覆盖 Host 的同名管道，冲突以 `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION` 拒绝。

rows: `'sync'`、`'async'`、`'generator'`、`'async-generator'`；决定 stage 及 run 返回类型。
`'single'` 或 `'multiple'`；直接采用 middleware-pipeline 的四模式继续及失败规则。
`'install'` 按分配顺序，`'reverse'` 按其逆序；同一插件在所有管道共享原排序 slot。

blocks.text: 持有函数 handle 的 owner 调用 `host.pipeline(name).use(stage)` 或 `.run(value, done)`；类 owner 使用 protected `pipeline(name)`。安装中的插件和 Feature core 只有 `use(stage)`、`through(name)` 登记权，没有 run。两种命名登记都返回带幂等 `remove()` 的句柄；移除影响后续运行，已取得的快照仍由原生命周期排空。

插件和它的 Feature 用原名访问 Host 管道、用短名访问自己的管道，并通过既有 Feature 依赖用 `插件名.管道名` 访问提供方的组。无依赖关系的插件不能访问别人的组。`IPluginHostCoreFor<typeof host>` 适合仅使用 Host 声明的 core；声明插件自己的管道时，保留 install 参数的推导，避免 Host-only 注解遮掉自己的短名。未知或不可见名字同步抛 `PIPELINE_UNKNOWN`；诊断包含查询的插件或 Feature、请求名和可见的 Host、本插件、依赖插件范围。

sync、generator 的命名 run 返回 `TResult | undefined`；async、async-generator 返回 `Promise<Awaited<TResult> | undefined>`。短路返回 undefined，每次到达末端的遍历各调用一次 done。multiple 不返回结果数组；需要每次结果时，在 done 中明确收集。multiple 模式下，stage 可以处理经 next 的 then/await 观察到的分支失败；未观察的失败仍由 runner 拒绝，多个原错按启动顺序保留在 `MULTIPLE_DOWNSTREAM_FAILED` 中。generator 用 throw 把失败交回 yield；sync 遍历全部登记值后汇总错误。

所有管道在同一 Host 事务中提交；每条管道在同一可见 stage 修订内复用编译快照，reverse 也只在编译时处理。没有可见 stage 时直接调用终点，不取快照或 lease。有 stage 时，所有管道复用同一套登记、排序和 quiescence/lease owner。安装失败回滚、unUse、replace、禁用和挂起在一次提交中作用于该插件的全部管道；已有运行持有原快照和分管道的代际 lease，drain 等待这些实际运行，清理和排空预算仍由既有生命周期配置控制。任何管道执行期间，owner 向任一管道注册 stage 都会抛 `PIPELINE_EXECUTING`。

Host 未声明 pipelines 时，其命名轴默认为 `Record<never, never>`；已知插件定义仍能推出其限定名。Host 和插件都没有命名组时，不分配额外的命名 runner、lane 或 lease key。原 `TValue`、`pipeline.mode`、四个 use*Pipeline、runPipeline/runPipelineSync/runPipelineAsync、pipelineMode 都只操作默认管道，原有显式泛型调用不变。默认管道使用内部 symbol，不占用任何字符串名字。显式填写 defineHost 泛型并同时声明命名管道时，要在第五个泛型参数传 `typeof pipelines`；省略它会保留空轴，pipeline(name) 只接受 never。

非法 map、名字、spec、order 以原生 TypeError / `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION` 在构造时拒绝，不返回 handle；mode 非法仍是 `INVALID_PIPELINE_MODE`。next 非法的外层码为 `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION`，cause 保留 middleware-pipeline 的 TypeError / `INVALID_OPTION`。spec 配置 getter 抛错时也以 `INVALID_PIPELINE_OPTION` 保留原 cause。

PluginHostError 继承 Error，携带只读 source、code、可选 detail；source 为 `plugin.host`，原始失败通过 cause/errors 可达。可写 native 回调错误原位附身份，不可写或非 Error 值保留在 cause，完整外包身份保留原 owner。INVALID_OPTION 形状错误保留 TypeError；配置值与循环错误是 PluginHostError。不要仅按类名处理所有错误，也不要解析诊断文案。

安装主错不被回滚失败覆盖。PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.detail 包含 failedName、按回滚顺序的 rollbackErrors；异步 use 的 detail 已完成且冻结，同步 useSync 先公布冻结快照，通过 detail.completion 返回最终冻结详情。需要完整次错身份的转换应先 await completion。回滚失败另报 PLUGIN_INSTALL_ROLLBACK_FAILED。

diagnostic 的第三参数保留原失败身份；诊断回调自身失败不会改变 Host 控制流，而交给 onDiagnosticFailure，再失败或省略时交给宿主存在的 globalThis.reportError。Node 需要这类观测时显式提供 onDiagnosticFailure。PluginHostStatus 为 active/closing/disposed；PluginHostRegistrationLifecycle 为 idle/install/dispose。ERROR_TEXT 是根命名导出的稳定英文消息表，MiddlewarePipelineMode/Violation 属于 middleware-pipeline。
`PluginHostDisposalNodeKind` 区分清理错误、聚合及 disposer 包装；`readPluginHostDisposalProvenance(error)` 只读取本物理包登记的追溯信息，未知错误或重复包副本返回 undefined，不按形状猜测。它用于诊断，不替代 source/code/cause 分类。

sections.content: Import openComposition from @migaia/plugin-host/composition, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use openComposition when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when openComposition does not match the required inputs or return contract.
